title: Supervised Single-Flight Opaque Cleanup Proof and Fenced Lookup Architecture for Telegram Storage Operation Reconciliation

dispositioned_findings: 124/125 cleanup does not locate commit boundary; lost response can follow durable COMMIT: addressed by mandatory post-cleanup database lookup separating process death from transaction outcome
126 and missing guardian exit cannot establish cleanup: addressed by strict failure-to-unknown; only verified clean guardian reap produces a witness
flock does not prove absence of SQLite fcntl/WAL writers: addressed by removing flock assertions; process death is established solely by observed supervisor/guardian reap
A caller-computed witness SHA256 is not trusted lifecycle observation: addressed by internally constructed opaque BEAM proof bound to observed process lifecycle
New native fence command adds unnecessary protocol and schema work: addressed by adopting the frozen v4 native protocol using clean cleanup followed by read_keys/lookup query

supervised_single_flight_owner.name: Supervised Single-Flight Database Owner
supervised_single_flight_owner.role: BEAM OTP actor/gen_server owning exclusive access to a given Telegram SQLite database configuration
rules: Prohibits duplicate concurrent in-flight operation dispatch to the same database
Serializes all native requests through the pinned guardian port
Maintains in-flight operation context: {operation_id, canonical_request_digest, expected_generation, dispatched_at_tick_us}
Transitions to RECONCILING state upon any uncertain return (timeout, port_close, DOWN, exit)
Blocks any subsequent mutation dispatch while in RECONCILING state until reconciliation reaches ReconciledCommitted or ReconciledAbsent

internal_opaque_cleanup_proof.name: Internally Constructed Opaque Cleanup Proof
internal_opaque_cleanup_proof.constructor: Minted exclusively inside telegram_store_transport from direct guardian port monitoring (never by caller)
internal_opaque_cleanup_proof.type_definition: {cleanup_witness, #{config_db_digest := Binary, native_bin_digest := Binary, guardian_bin_digest := Binary, operation_id := Binary, operation_digest := Binary, exit_status := Int, reaped_at_us := Int}}

valid_witness_produced: Guardian process exited with verified code 124 (timeout with clean SIGKILL reap of child process tree confirmed)
Guardian process exited with verified code 125 (buffer overflow with clean SIGKILL reap of child process tree confirmed)
witness_strictly_refused: Guardian exited with code 126 (SIGTERM timeout where child did not cleanly terminate within grace period)
Guardian exited with code 127 or unhandled signal
Port closed or DOWN without clean guardian exit message
Any mismatched configuration, database path, or operation digest

internal_opaque_cleanup_proof.handling_of_refusal: Returns {reconciled_unknown, <<"writer_quiescence_unproven">>}; state remains held for supervisor restart/cgroup recovery

cleanup_then_lookup_reconciliation_proto.name: Two-Phase Cleanup-Then-Lookup Reconciliation
phase_1_quiescence_verification: 1. Supervised owner observes uncertain response on an in-flight operation.
3. If guardian lifecycle did not cleanly reap the worker (e.g. exit 126, crash, missing message): owner halts with {reconciled_unknown, <<"writer_quiescence_unproven">>}.

4. If guardian lifecycle confirms complete process-tree reap (exit 124/125): transport mints the internal opaque CleanupWitness bound to {config_db_digest, native_bin_digest, operation_id, operation_digest}.
phase_2_fenced_state_lookup: 1. Owner launches a fresh, clean read query through the transport to the database using the frozen v4 wire protocol.
2. Query inspects the durable receipt table for the specific operation_id.

3. Scenario A (Post-Commit Lost Response): The receipt row exists in SQLite with matching operation_id and canonical digest. Outcome: ReconciledCommitted(Receipt). Durable state transition is recovered intact; caller is provided the original commit receipt.

4. Scenario B (Timeout Before Commit): The receipt row is absent in SQLite. Because CleanupWitness proves the prior worker was fully reaped before this query, no background write can occur. Outcome: ReconciledAbsent(CleanupWitness). Operation is proven non-committed.

5. Scenario C (Decode Failure on Lookup): If the returned response fails domain decoding, transport retains the cleanup evidence and operation context in an explicit wrapped error {error, {domain_decode_failure, Detail, Context, CleanupWitness}} without dropping lifecycle evidence.

side_effect_and_retry_fencing.name: Zero-Blind-Retry and Side-Effect Policy
side_effect_and_retry_fencing.mandate: ReconciledAbsent proves the absence of storage commitment, but NEVER automatically initiates an external HTTP send or blind retry.
side_effect_and_retry_fencing.policy: Any retry decision belongs strictly to the higher-level service supervisor (L3) under explicit rate-limiting and authorization policies. No implicit re-submission within the storage client.

formal_invariants.statement: An operation cannot be reconciled as ReconciledAbsent without a valid internally constructed CleanupWitness proving zero surviving worker processes.
A CleanupWitness can only be minted from verified guardian exit codes 124 or 125 with confirmed process tree reap; code 126, unhandled signals, or missing exits strictly fail to unproven quiescence.

A CleanupWitness is cryptographically bound to the database path digest, native executable digest, guardian executable digest, operation ID, and canonical operation digest. Any argument mismatch is refused.
Absence of a receipt in SQLite proves non-commitment ONLY when evaluated after a verified CleanupWitness is established; lookup alone without prior writer quiescence remains ReconciledUnknown.
The database owner enforces single-flight serialization: no subsequent operation can be dispatched to a database while an earlier operation is undergoing reconciliation.
Domain decode failures on returned responses must retain the associated cleanup witness and operation context rather than dropping them into opaque errors.

acceptance_matrix.expected_behavior: Guardian exits 124, child process tree reaped, lookup finds no receipt -> Reconciles as ReconciledAbsent(CleanupWitness)
Transport experiences disconnect/timeout, guardian reaps worker, lookup finds committed receipt -> Reconciles as ReconciledCommitted(Receipt)

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Wrong database, operation digest, or configuration
acceptance_matrix.expected_behavior: Transport or store refuses proof validation with {error, {store_invariant_error, <<"quiescence_witness_binding_mismatch">>}}

acceptance_matrix.scenario: Unknown cleanup (exit 126, crash, missing guardian message)
acceptance_matrix.expected_behavior: Witness is refused; reconciliation yields {reconciled_unknown, <<"writer_quiescence_unproven">>}; database owner remains held until supervisor intervention
After cleanup and absence reconciliation, worker/group markers remain absent and generation CAS remains consistent
